sources.title: InsideEVs - Hyundai Ioniq 5 fast charging analysis (Battery Life test, Seoul, 2021-04-20)
sources.notes: 2021 Ioniq 5 AWD 77 kWh (72.6 net), 800 V charger at Hyundai EV Station Gangdong, 19 C ambient, 15 C battery at start (article estimate). Chart is an image; values taken from the article text and are approximate.

sources.title: InsideEVs - Hyundai Ioniq 5 with 58 kWh pack: in-depth charging analysis (Battery Life, IONITY)
sources.notes: 2021 Ioniq 5 AWD with the 58 kWh pack, IONITY, 16 C ambient, tester Andreas Haehnel (Battery Life). Values from the article text, approximate (article warns of >5 % uncertainty).

sources.title: InsideEVs - Kia EV6 prototype fast charging analysis (Out of Spec Reviews data, 2021-09-29)
sources.notes: Pre-production EV6 AWD prototype, 77.4 kWh, tested in Germany at IONITY with a preconditioned battery by Kyle Conner (Out of Spec Reviews). Values from the article text; some chart values were estimated by the article.

curves.notes: 2023 model year Ioniq 5 AWD 77.4 kWh, preconditioned via navigation, Alpitronic HYC300 (EnBW Lauenau, winter 2023, single-digit temperatures; 4 C is the ambient stated at the outbound stop). Session started at 19 %. Text values only (113 kW at 19 %, ~195 kW plateau, 224 kW from 40 % held to 55 %, 125 kW at 80 %); the 25 % point is where the ~195 kW stage begins, an approximate reading. Sparse (5 points). Software from 2023 changed the curve above 80 % per the article, so older 2022 cars may differ. Shape agrees with InsideEVs/Battery Life (peak plateau ~225 kW to about 50 %).

Launch-era (2021) Ioniq 5 AWD, 800 V charger in Seoul (350 kW per Hyundai demo, not stated by the tester), 10-80 % session. Values read from the article text: ~115 kW at 10 %, 187 kW at 14-15 %, ~220 kW at 29-30 %, >225 kW around 51 %, a dip to ~120 kW at 52-54 %, recovery to ~170 kW, ~130 kW at 79-80 %. The 55 % point is the article reading of "after 54 %". Sparse (7). Peak 225 kW matches the electrive test 224 kW plateau.

curves.notes: 2021 Ioniq 5 AWD with the 58 kWh pack on IONITY (rated power not stated). Values from the article text: ~177 kW peak from about 7 % to 45 %, a drop below 145 kW from 45 to 57 % (~140 kW), a temporary dip near 60 %, then a decline to ~50 kW at 86 %; 20-80 % average 144 kW. Sparse (5 points); stated peak is 1 % above the 175 kW dc_max. Battery temperature not reported.

curves.notes: Out of Spec Reviews 0-100 % test of a PRE-PRODUCTION EV6 AWD prototype (77.4 kWh) in Germany on IONITY, preconditioned, as analysed by InsideEVs. Plateau ~233 kW (234 peak) to ~46 %, then a volatile taper with a dip to ~30 kW at 63 %, brief recovery to ~190 kW at 66 %, ~6 kW held at 82 % for about 4 minutes. The article calls the curve quirky; production software may differ, so treat the mid-curve dips as prototype behaviour. Text values only (the 2 % point is ">200 kW", entered as 205). Ambient not stated. Peak 233 kW is below the 240 kW dc_max. A production EV6 in Nyland 1000 km test reached over 230 kW (InsideEVs, 6 C), agreeing on the peak.

Tested on a 2024 EV9 GT-Line AWD, 99.8 kWh pack, carried over to 2026 (same pack; 2026 changes the port to NACS, no pack change found). Points read from article text, not a table. Conditions: Electrify America 350 kW, Northern California; temperature not stated. First point is about 200 kW almost immediately (test started near 18%). Session was interrupted once and restarted. Applied to every EV9 on the 99.8 kWh 800 V pack (2024-2027): same pack and DC hardware; 2026+ changes the port to NACS only. InsideEVs states a ~215 kW peak; other reports of the same pack give up to ~234 kW, so peak varies with charger.

Sparse (3 points) EverTV test of a 2026 IONIQ 9, trim not stated; shape between points is a straight-line assumption. Peak 235 kW at 60%. Car did not allow preconditioning. Electrek measured a lower peak (~215 kW) on a different charger; InsideEVs relays 243 kW with no SoC points. Timer started at 10% after arriving at 5%. Applied to all three 2026 trims (same 110.3 kWh 800 V pack). Electrek (Calligraphy) saw ~215 kW peak and 197.75 kW at 60 %; InsideEVs relays 243 kW (The Ioniq Guy, 350 kW Electrify America); Torque News 218 kW peak on a 16-80 % Electrify Canada session; none give SoC points.
